surface_verification.justification: The only runtime surface in this diff is the dompurify bump, because dompurify is mermaid's sanitizer. The repo's MermaidRenderer.test.tsx does vi.mock("mermaid"), so the entire existing suite is structurally blind to a sanitizer regression — passing unit tests would have proven nothing here. Verified instead in real Chromium: esbuild-bundled the ACTUALLY INSTALLED mermaid 11.16.0 + dompurify 3.4.12, rendered a flowchart with the app's own securityLevel:"strict", and asserted absolute expectations (SVG present, 16283 chars, 340x501px, all 5 node labels, 0 surviving <script>, 0 console errors) -> PASS. Verified LOAD-BEARING by degrading the render and re-running: FAILED (exit 1). HONEST LIMITATION: this was an authoring-time probe, not a committed spec — the repo still has no permanent real-mermaid rendering coverage, which is recorded as follow-up 3 in the iterate spec rather than absorbed silently.
